land.text: Odisha, ending the Eastern Ganga dynasty in 1434-1435

predecessors.note: The sa-03 dossier of the Eastern Gangas ends 1434 and names the successor 'suryavamsha-dynasty'; that slug should read gajapati-kingdom.

successors.note: A guess at the slug: the page names the usurper but no dynasty. A dossier is needed.

capitals.name: Kataka (Cuttack)
capitals.note: 'Their capital was Kataka'; the page does not date its adoption. Kapilendra was crowned at Bhubaneswar (20.27 N, 85.84 E) on 29 June 1435. Rajahmundry was the southern governor's seat.

rulers.name: Hamvira Deva
rulers.note: Elder son of Kapilendra; reign 1472-1476 from the infobox of the Gajapati page.

rulers.name: Purushottama Deva (restored)
rulers.note: The start of the second reign is bridged to the end of Hamvira's; he died 1497 at Kataka.

rulers.note: The infobox table is garbled; 'Kalua Deva' also appears.

region.text: Odisha, the Eastern Ganga heartland, capital Kataka

ledger.note: 1434: the Gajapati kingdom begins in Odisha. Infobox '1434-1541'; 'founded by Kapilendra Deva of Suryavamsa lineage'; Kapilendra's page: 'Reign: 1434 - 25 November 1466', coronation '29 June 1435, Bhubaneswar', the ascension 'through a coup or rebellion'. The page gives no boundary.

region.text: territories of Bengal west of the Ganga, including the fort of Gar Mandaran

ledger.note: 1447: Kapilendra takes Bengal west of the Ganga. 'The Gopinathpur inscription of 1447 CE describes his campaign against the Sultan of Bengal'; 'The Gajapati army conquered territories of Bengal to the west of Ganga river including the fort of Gar Mandaran'. (A Jagannath temple inscription of 1450 narrates 'the conquest of Gauda', not drawn.)

1448: Rajahmundry under Kapilendra. 'The kingdom of Rajahmundry was thus brought under the sway of Kapilendra before A. D. 1448.' The Reddy page: Rajahmundry 'was conquered by the Gajapatis some 25 years later' than 1424; its Reddi branch dates from 1395 and the kingdom to 1448.

1453: Kapilendra's army crosses the Krishna. 'After August 1453, Kapilendra's army crossed the Krishna and occupied Kondavidu'; 'by A.D. 1454 Kapilendra had become the master of the former Reddi kingdoms of Rajahmundry and Kondavidu'. The Reddy page has Kondavidu annexed by Vijayanagara in 1424, so the loser is read as Vijayanagara.

region.text: the southern states of Udayagiri and Chandragiri

ledger.note: 1460: Hamvira's general takes Udayagiri and Chandragiri. 'Hamvira Deva's general Tamavupala conquered the southern states of Udayagiri and Chandragiri in the year 1460 CE'; the page names Vijayanagara under Mallikarjuna Raya as the enemy elsewhere, so the loser is read as Vijayanagara.

1472: the Bahmanis take Rajahmundry and Kondavidu in the civil war. 'The Turko-Persian Bahamanis had equally captured the southern parts of the Gajapati Empire named as Rajamahendravaram and Kondavidu.' The page gives no year; Purushottama's first reign ended in October 1472, the bridging year.

1472: Saluva Narasimha takes Udayagiri and Chandragiri. 'General named Ishwara Nayaka captured the Udayagiri fort from the Gajapati forces stationed there' (during the civil war); no year on the page, so the end of the first reign is used.

1476: Udayagiri and Chandragiri return. They 'were later returned to the Gajapatis in exchange for Saluva Narasimha's release' after the Kanchi expedition ('In the second attempt Kanchi was captured, Saluva Narasimha was defeated'); the page gives no year, so the start of Purushottama's second reign is the bridging year.

region.text: the Krishna river basin: Rajahmundry, Kondavidu and Kondapalli

ledger.note: 1500: Prataparudra reaches the Krishna. He 'reached the banks of river Krishna on 4 November 1500 AD' and the Anantakarma grant says he 'was able to capture the Krishna river basin with the use of force'; the former holder is not named on the page and the Purushottama page has the Bahmanis holding Rajahmundry and Kondapalli.
1512: Vijayanagara besieges Udayagiri. 'The Vijayanagara army laid siege to the Udayagiri fort in 1512.' The campaign 'lasted for a year before the Gajapati army disintegrated due to starvation'.
1514: Udayagiri surrenders. 'Since no help reached to the Gajapati forces, they had to surrender finally in the year 1514.'

region.text: Udayagiri, with Chandragiri by my reading

ledger.note: 1514: Udayagiri is lost to Vijayanagara. The surrender is dated 1514 on the Prataparudra page, which does not name the besieger; the Krishnadevaraya page has the Vijayanagara army besieging it from 1512 (a year, which does not square with 1514). [Reviewer sa-04-x, 2026-10-19: confidence 3 to 2: the Prataparudra page names Udayagiri ('they had to surrender finally in the year 1514') but not Chandragiri or the Tirupati circle, nor the besieger]

1516: Krishnadevaraya takes Kondavidu. 'It was taken by the Vijayanagara emperor Krishnadevaraya in 1516'; the Krishnadevaraya page adds 'the capture of the fort and the imprisonment of Prince Virabhadra, the son of Prataparudra Deva' and that Prataparudra was 'driven to Cuttack'. The lands north of the Krishna were returned afterwards (undated).

region.text: Kondapalli and the forts of the southern parts

ledger.note: 1531: Quli Qutb Shah takes Kondapalli. 'Quli Qutb Shah invaded southern parts of Odisha and captured many forts along with the regional administrative center of Kondapalli on 20 March 1531'; 'he also lost many large portions of his territory in the south'. [Reviewer sa-04-x, 2026-10-19: confidence 3 to 2: the page names Kondapalli and 'many forts' in 'southern parts of Odisha', not Rajahmundry, which the region includes]

region.text: Odisha and the Bengal strip, taken by Govinda Vidyadhara

ledger.note: 1541: the Gajapati line ends in Odisha. Infobox '1434-1541'; 'His successors were murdered by the treacherous Govinda Vidyadhara after his death' (Prataparudra died in 1540) and the rulers table ends with Khakharua Deva, 1540-1541. The page names no successor state.

wars.name: Gajapati-Bengal war

zones.text: Bengal west of the Ganga to Gar Mandaran

wars.outcome: The Gajapatis took the territory west of the Ganga in 1447; a Puri inscription of 1450 narrates the conquest of Gauda, which is not drawn.

wars.name: Kapilendra's conquest of the Reddi kingdoms
wars.outcome: Rajahmundry was Kapilendra's before 1448 and Kondavidu after August 1453; by 1454 he was master of both.
wars.note: 'The Odia forces returned in the year 1446 CE led by the Prince Hamvira Deva' (the page does not name the target).

wars.name: Gajapati-Bahmani wars
wars.outcome: A battle at Devarakonda in 1458 and a 'significant military campaign' in 1461; no territory is dated.

wars.name: Gajapati civil war

zones.text: the south, lost to the Bahmanis and Saluva Narasimha

wars.outcome: Purushottama lost more than half of his father's empire to Hamvira and the Bahmanis; Udayagiri and Chandragiri came back after the Kanchi expedition.

wars.name: Vijayanagara-Gajapati war
wars.outcome: Udayagiri surrendered in 1514, Kondavidu fell in 1516 and the lands north of the Krishna were returned, making the river the frontier.

wars.name: Qutb Shahi invasion of the Gajapati south
wars.outcome: Quli Qutb Shah took Kondapalli on 20 March 1531 with many forts of the south.

certainty.note: No treaty line is named on any page opened; the Krishna as the boundary with Vijayanagara after the war of 1512-1516 is the nearest to a fixed line and is undated.

notes:
No Cliopatria row. Seven pages (Gajapati Kingdom, Kapilendra Deva, Purushottama Deva, Prataparudra Deva, Krishnadevaraya, Kondavidu Fort, Reddy Kingdom). The Gajapati page is thin (garbled rulers table, no area, no capital date). The pages give no area, so every keyframe is a reading from the towns they name; circles stand for forts.
Slug: the sa-03 dossier eastern-ganga-kingdom names its successor 'suryavamsha-dynasty'; this dossier is gajapati-kingdom (Wikipedia title), and the successor link should be changed.
Disagreements: Kapilendra died 25 November 1466 (infobox) against 1467 in the succession table; Udayagiri besieged 1512 for 'a year' (Krishnadevaraya page) against surrender 'in the year 1514' (Prataparudra page); Kondavidu Reddi dates 1325-1424 (Reddy page) against 1328-1428 and a Reddi capital 'between 1328 and 1482' (Kondavidu Fort page).
Not settled: when Hamvira's army returned in 1446 and against whom; the Bahmani wars of 1458 and 1461 (no result on the page); the far south ('Trichinapalli, Tanjore and Arcot', undated, not drawn); the dates of the Bahmani and Saluva losses and returns (bridged at confidence 1 to 1472 and 1476); the date of the peace with Krishnadevaraya and of the return of the lands north of the Krishna; Chandragiri in 1514; the northern frontier with Bengal under Hussain Shah (the Prataparudra page says only 'minor skirmishes continued'); Gauda 1450 (a raid); the end of the Bengal strip; the 1541 successor.
Counterparts needing a dossier: reddi-kingdom (written in this batch if reached), vijayanagara-empire and bahmani-sultanate (sa-04-c), sultanate-of-bengal (sa-04-c), golconda-sultanate (sa-04-d), bhoi-dynasty (the usurper Govinda Vidyadhara's line, Odisha 1541 onwards).
